captain.description: Read concise summaries of work you own across the organization; unfinished only by default. Use the returned id/revision to update progress. Fetch long goals and acceptance criteria with work_item_get only when needed.

after.description: The previous page's nextAfter global plan ID; omitted starts the first page.

include_finished.description: true also includes done/dropped plans; default false.

include_removed.description: true also reads work in removed crews, default false. Objects with frozen:true are read-only; do not repeatedly try to advance them.

captain.name: my_work_items

captain.description: Read details by global plan ID. Organization work is readable, including removed crews. Reading does not wake anyone.

id.description: Global W ID returned by a work tool, not a legacy crew-local alias.

captain.name: work_item_get

captain.description: Register real planned work, owned by you by default. Set the actual goal, completion level and acceptance criteria. Parent/dependency links currently require the same crew. State, events, identity and progress commit together. Retain the returned id/revision; do not duplicate a plan to retry an unknown outcome.

acceptance.description: How to judge that completion level was achieved.

crew.description: Crew number, ID or unique name, defaults to your crew. Target crew authority is checked independently.

depends_on.description: Global W IDs of dependencies in the same crew.

goal.description: The actual goal; detail is loaded on demand.

next_check_at.description: RFC3339 check time; active work must have a valid next check.

owner.description: Owner session ID, defaults to you. Assigning someone else requires captain authority.

parent.description: The same crew parent's global W ID.

sources.description: Global # IDs of registered original requirements.

title.description: Clearly state what this item will accomplish.

captain.name: work_item_create

captain.description: Report progress or completion using the revision you just read; stale revisions cannot overwrite new work. Progress requires a next-step note and active requires a valid check time. The owner marks done; evidence is optional, with no extra verification gate. On conflict read the latest summary/detail and reassess rather than blindly looping.

evidence.description: Optional completion evidence: {kind:"commit"|"url"|"text", value:"nonblank text"}; only for done.

expected_revision.description: The revision string from a summary or the previous operation, passed unchanged.

next_check_at.description: RFC3339 check time, later than now and within work limits; not accepted for done.

note.description: Overwrite this item's next-step/progress note; required and nonblank except for completion.

status.description: open/active/done; omitted updates only the note/check time. Blocking, dropping and transfer are separate actions.

captain.name: work_item_update

captain.description:
Post key moments to a channel: started, done, blocked, handing off, important findings. Write the conclusion in one sentence plus the one thing you need decided; long tables and lists go into a file, post the path. Keep terminal detail (what you read or ran) out of channels.
Say where it goes; there is no default: channel = post in a channel; to = a dm with one session by its directory number (also across crews); reply_to alone = the channel of that message. With none of the three you get an error listing your channels.
@ only wakes people. Without an @, nobody is woken (except sessions listening to the channel). In a dm, the other side is always woken. @session / @captain wake the named agents; @human flags the message for the human. Use @human only to ask a question (use ask when the human needs to decide), never to report progress. Whoever you @, everyone who can read the channel sees the message. @human in a channel the human is not watching may be seen much later: for anything urgent post in your home (top-level crew) human channel, and use ask for a decision.
Posting too fast, repeating the same text, or @human too often is held back (the receipt says what to do): merge your updates into one message.
The receipt predicts whom the post will wake under current membership and listens; prediction does not mean it was queued, delivered or started working. A message body is at most 256 KiB.

category.description: What this is: progress / done / blocked / question / finding / handoff / ack / note.

channel.description: Channel id, or a channel name that is unique among the channels you can read. Not together with to.

mentions.description: Who to wake: {kind:"session", target_id:"<session id or directory number>"} / {kind:"captain"} / {kind:"human"}. Without an @, nobody is woken (except sessions listening to the channel). In a dm, the other side is still woken. Everyone who can read the channel still sees it. A mentioned session must be a member of the channel; @captain likewise requires the captain to be a member, and @captain in a crew without a captain is an error.

message.description: Use for a single message. Mutually exclusive with messages.

messages.description: Several messages at once (at most 6), one bubble each with its own category. If any item is invalid nothing is posted and the error names the item. mentions and reply_to apply to the first message only.

reply_to.description: The message you are replying to: its number (#128 or 128) or its id. Same channel only. The original sender is mentioned automatically (while still in the channel): all channel members still see it, the sender is woken; replying to your own message or to a system message adds no mention.

to.description: A dm with one session by its directory number: 7-3 (crew 7, extension 3), 7 (crew 7's current captain), 0 (the management crew's captain); look numbers up with directory. A pair has one dm, reused when it exists. The human has no dm (to: "human" points you to your home human channel): reach the human there, and use ask for a decision. Not together with channel or reply_to.

captain.name: post

captain.description: Read a channel page by page (oldest first). Use it for older messages or for channels you are not in. Reading up to the newest message marks the channel read for you, so those messages are not injected again — only for channels you are in or listen to (reading other channels does not move your read position). The #number before each message can go into reply_to.

before.description: Only messages before this one (number or id). Omitted = newest page.

channel.description: Channel id or name; omitted = your crew's lobby. Readable: your crew's channels (dms between its members included — there are no private channels), your home human channel, channels you are in or listen to; management crew sessions read the whole organisation.

captain.name: read_channel

captain.description: Search messages in the channels you can read, to find something said earlier (your crew's channels, your home human channel, channels you are in or listen to, archived ones included; management crew sessions search the whole organisation). The whole trimmed query is matched as ONE case-insensitive substring (ASCII case folding only), not split into terms; newest first.

after.description: Only at or after this time (ISO8601).

before.description: Only strictly before this time (ISO8601, exclusive: created_at < before).

channel.description: Search only this channel (id or name).

crew.description: Search only that crew's channels you can read (crew number, id or name).

query.description: The text to find: trimmed, then matched as one substring (ASCII case-insensitive).

captain.name: search

captain.description: List channels, to find a channel id or see which channels the human is watching: first your home human channel (post there what the human must see), then channels you are in or listen to, the other channels of your crew, and channels the human is watching. Each row: id · name · type · purpose · owner · members · state (member / listening / human watching / archived / you own it).

crew.description: List only that crew's channels you can read (crew number, id or name).

include_archived.description: true = include archived channels; they are left out by default.

captain.name: list_channels

captain.description: Create a topic channel. Use it whenever you need to collaborate with someone on something or discuss a topic separately — do not create a child crew for that. You become the owner and a member. Give it a name and a purpose, e.g. "release", "scroll bug". A name equal to the human labels (人类 / Human) or to crewd's own system labels is rejected. A dm needs no creating: post(to:) opens one when there is none yet.

members.description: Members to add right away (optional; channel_invite later works too): session ids, directory numbers (like 7-3; 7 = crew 7's current captain), or human. Leave yourself out.

purpose.description: One sentence: what the channel is for.

captain.name: channel_create

captain.description: Add members to a channel, when others should follow or discuss the matter too. Usually you must be a member yourself; the lobby and a dm cannot take invites.

members.description: Session ids, directory numbers (like 7-3), or human.

captain.name: channel_invite

captain.description: Leave a channel, when its matter no longer concerns you. You cannot leave the lobby; a dm cannot be left (archive it instead); the owner of a topic channel must hand ownership on with channel_owner first.
captain.name: channel_leave

captain.description: Archive a channel when its matter is done (messages kept, no new posts; the human can unarchive). Only the owner, the captain of the channel's crew or the human can archive; the lobby and the human channel cannot be archived.
captain.name: channel_archive

captain.description: Channel ownership. The owner acts as the channel's captain: when the human posts without naming anyone, the owner is usually the one woken and takes it — answers, or hands it to the right person. Three uses: with to = the owner offers it (you mention them in the channel under your own name; it takes effect once they call channel_owner(channel=…)); without to = accept an ownership offered to you; with to and force=true = the captain of the channel's crew (the management captain counts) moves it at once, without acceptance. The new owner must be a member.

force.description: For captains, together with to: true = move ownership without waiting for acceptance.

to.description: New owner: session id or directory number (like 7-3). Omitted = accept the ownership offered to you.

captain.name: channel_owner

captain.description: Listen to a channel: new messages there wake you even without a mention. Use it while waiting for activity; end your turn normally while listening instead of polling read_channel. Only channels you can read can be listened to. Stop with channel_listen(channel=…, off=true).

minutes.description: How long (minutes, 1–480). Omitted = until you stop it with off=true.

off.description: true = stop listening to this channel (not together with minutes or senders). Not listening already is not an error.

senders.description: Only these senders: human; captain (whoever holds that role when posting, so this follows captain changes); or a session id or directory number (resolved once—for example, 7-1 resolves to crew 7's current captain and does not follow later changes). This affects only whose messages wake you; all messages in the channel are still injected. Omitted = everyone.

captain.name: channel_listen

captain.description: Use the directory to find someone or talk across crews. Every crew and session on this machine has a short number: crews are integers (7), members are extensions (7-3), 7-1 is crew 7's current captain, and 0 is the management crew (0 = its current captain). Each row: number, name, crew or parent path, session id. Numbers go straight into post's to (a dm, across crews too) and into member arguments of the tools. Channels are listed by list_channels; the human has no number: post what the human must see in your home human channel, and use ask for a decision.

query.description: Filter by number prefix, name or org path; omitted = everything.

captain.name: directory

captain.description: Use it when the human has to decide: ask the human a question (workers too — not a post in the human channel). Non-blocking: the question becomes a pending item (an H number), is posted to your home (top-level crew; the management crew is its own home) human channel mentioning the human, and you get a receipt right away — go do something else or end your turn. When the human answers you are woken and resume_note is read back to you verbatim.

fallback.description: What you will do if nobody answers in time ("go with A"). Give together with fallback_after_minutes.

fallback_after_minutes.description: Optional: if nobody answers within this many minutes, you are woken to act on fallback. Only for reversible things.

question.description: The decision you need. State the options and your preference — "A / B, I lean A because …".

resume_note.description: What you will do once answered (where you are, what is next). Always write it for questions asked mid-task.

captain.name: ask

captain.description: Withdraw an unanswered question that no longer applies. You can withdraw your own; the captain can withdraw any in the crew (the management crew's captain counts as the captain of every crew). A question still blocking a work item cannot be withdrawn.

crew.description: Whose book holds the question (crew number or id); omitted = your own crew.

reason.description: Why it no longer applies: what changed.

captain.name: withdraw_ask

captain.description: Respond to an item in your crew's Agent Todo list (work the human gave the crew): when you claim it, when there is progress, and when it is done. Append-only; does not change status.
captain.name: respond_todo

captain.description: Subscription usage for claude / codex on this machine: percent used per window and reset times. Check before long work. There is no absolute remaining token count; do not invent one.
captain.name: get_quota

captain.description: Wake yourself later: at the time, note is delivered back to you. When quota runs low: wrap up to a hand-off state, schedule a few minutes after the reset, stop. When you wake you only have the note and channel messages, so make the note self-contained.

after_minutes.description: Minutes from now (1–1440). Either this or at.

at.description: An RFC 3339 time carrying the offset you mean (like 2026-10-08T09:00:00+08:00; Z = UTC), in the future and at most 7 days ahead. Either this or after_minutes.

note.description: What to do on waking and where the context is.

captain.name: schedule_wakeup

captain.description: Switch your own model or reasoning effort. Not immediate: this changes the session's setting, which takes effect the next time the session starts (restart or resume); the current turn is unchanged. Use the most expensive tier only when normal tiers clearly fail.

model.description: Model alias such as opus / sonnet.

captain.name: set_session_profile

captain.description: Give the crew a short label like "auth refactor". Do it once you know what the crew is doing. crew omitted = this crew; another crew only if you act as its captain.

crew.description: Optional: which crew (number or id); omitted = this crew.

captain.name: rename_crew

captain.description: Change crews' working directory. Call without confirm for a preview, then with confirm: true. You may change a crew you act as captain of (the management crew's captain: any crew) and the crews below yours. Removed crews are left alone.

crew.description: Optional: which crew (number or id); omitted = this crew.

include_children.description: Also change child crews; default true.

new_path.description: Absolute path of an existing directory.

captain.name: change_workdir

captain.description: One sentence on how the whole crew is doing, shown on the crew's sidebar row; update it when things change. Over 200 characters is refused; an empty string clears it. crew omitted = this crew.

crew.description: Optional: which crew (number or id); omitted = this crew.

captain.name: set_crew_status

captain.description: The crew's delegation policy: read it before handing out work; replace it when the policy changes. Without text = read it; with text = replace it with that text. crew omitted = this crew.

crew.description: Optional: which crew (number or id); omitted = this crew.

text.description: Optional: the full new text (replaces the old one); omitted = read only.

captain.name: delegation_policy

captain.description: Start a worker for a clear coding task. crew omitted = this crew; another crew only if you act as its captain (the management crew's captain counts as the captain of every crew).

brief.description: The task, with goal and done criteria.

crew.description: Optional: the crew to start it in (number or id); omitted = this crew.

isolation.description: Required. false = use the crew's shared directory; true = create a separate git worktree for it. Decide per call from parallel conflicts, change scope and how the tasks relate; if creation fails you get an error, never a silent fallback to the shared directory.

runner.description: claude or codex; omitted = crew default.

title.description: At most 18 characters, no project name; the worker's display name. Omitted = the first 18 characters of the brief's first line.

captain.name: start_session

captain.description: Stop a session's process: the reason is posted in your name to its crew's lobby first, then it is stopped; irreversible. To interrupt one turn only, nudge_session with esc. You cannot stop yourself.

reason.description: Why; posted publicly to the lobby.

session_id.description: Target session: id or directory number (like 7-3).

captain.name: stop_session

captain.description: See a session's state and recent terminal output (codex: transcript tail). Use it when a mention gets no answer.

session_id.description: Target session: id or directory number (like 7-3).

captain.name: inspect_session

captain.description: Interrupt a session's current turn: only the keys esc / interrupt. To tell it something, post(to: …) to it; it reads that when woken. Sending is not confirmation: inspect_session a few seconds later to see the effect.

key.description: esc or interrupt; both interrupt its current turn.

session_id.description: Target session: id or directory number (like 7-3).

captain.name: nudge_session

captain.description: List a crew's sessions (id, number, name, role, state), before handing out work or to find a session. crew omitted = this crew.

crew.description: Optional: crew number or id; omitted = this crew.

captain.name: list_sessions

captain.description: Hand over a crew's captain role: to_session hands it to an existing session (which must belong to that crew), or runner starts a new session to take over; give exactly one. crew omitted = this crew; it may also be a direct child crew of yours, or any crew you act as captain of. The old captain stays in the crew as a worker.

crew.description: Optional: whose captain role (crew number or id); omitted = this crew.

effort.description: Optional: the new captain's reasoning effort (with runner only).

model.description: Optional: the new captain's model (with runner only).

opening_brief.description: Optional: the new captain's first task (with runner only).

runner.description: Start a new session to take over: claude or codex.

title.description: Optional: the new captain's display name, at most 18 characters; omitted = Captain (with runner only).

to_session.description: The successor: an existing session's id or directory number; it must belong to that crew.

captain.name: handoff_captain

captain.description: Change where crews sit in the organisation tree. action is one of five: create_child (a new child crew under crew: it inherits the working directory and gets its own captain started, whose first task is brief); create_parent (a new parent crew above crew, with its own captain started); adopt (put target under crew); adopt_parent (put crew under target); release (detach crew's direct child target, optionally moving it under to; with no other parent left it becomes top-level). New or adopted crews go at the end of their siblings. Removing, restoring, purging and ordering crews are the human's and are not here. Child crews only express organisational structure — a lasting department or team with its own captain. To collaborate on a topic or a task, create a channel with channel_create instead. crew omitted = this crew; another crew only if you act as its captain.

action.description: One of create_child / create_parent / adopt / adopt_parent / release.

brief.description: Required for create_child: the child crew captain's first task, with goal and done criteria.

crew.description: Optional: the crew acted on (number or id); omitted = this crew.

runner.description: Optional, create_child only: claude or codex for the child crew's captain; omitted = default.

target.description: Required for adopt / adopt_parent / release: the other crew (number or id). The target of adopt / adopt_parent and the to of release must be a crew you act as captain of, or a direct child of one; moving crews across other branches of the tree is an organisation-level change: ask the management crew's captain (post(to: "0")) or the human.

title.description: Optional, for create_child / create_parent: the new crew's short label; omitted = from a template.

to.description: Optional, release only: where to move target (the same reach as target: a crew you act as captain of, or a direct child of one).

captain.name: crew_structure

worker.description: Use the directory to find someone or talk across crews. Every crew and session on this machine has a short number: crews are integers (7), members are extensions (7-3), 7-1 is crew 7's current captain, and 0 is the management crew (0 = its current captain). Each row: number, name, crew or parent path, session id. Numbers go straight into post's to (a dm, across crews too) and into member arguments of the tools. Channels are listed by list_channels; the human has no number: post what the human must see in your home human channel, and use ask for a decision.

query.description: Filter by number prefix, name or org path; omitted = everything.

worker.name: directory

worker.description: Use it when the human has to decide: ask the human a question (workers too — not a post in the human channel). Non-blocking: the question becomes a pending item (an H number), is posted to your home (top-level crew; the management crew is its own home) human channel mentioning the human, and you get a receipt right away — go do something else or end your turn. When the human answers you are woken and resume_note is read back to you verbatim.

fallback.description: What you will do if nobody answers in time ("go with A"). Give together with fallback_after_minutes.

fallback_after_minutes.description: Optional: if nobody answers within this many minutes, you are woken to act on fallback. Only for reversible things.

question.description: The decision you need. State the options and your preference — "A / B, I lean A because …".

resume_note.description: What you will do once answered (where you are, what is next). Always write it for questions asked mid-task.

worker.name: ask

worker.description: Withdraw an unanswered question that no longer applies. You can withdraw your own; the captain can withdraw any in the crew (the management crew's captain counts as the captain of every crew). A question still blocking a work item cannot be withdrawn.

crew.description: Whose book holds the question (crew number or id); omitted = your own crew.

reason.description: Why it no longer applies: what changed.

worker.name: withdraw_ask

worker.description: Respond to an item in your crew's Agent Todo list (work the human gave the crew): when you claim it, when there is progress, and when it is done. Append-only; does not change status.
worker.name: respond_todo

worker.description: Subscription usage for claude / codex on this machine: percent used per window and reset times. Check before long work. There is no absolute remaining token count; do not invent one.
worker.name: get_quota

worker.description: Wake yourself later: at the time, note is delivered back to you. When quota runs low: wrap up to a hand-off state, schedule a few minutes after the reset, stop. When you wake you only have the note and channel messages, so make the note self-contained.

after_minutes.description: Minutes from now (1–1440). Either this or at.

at.description: An RFC 3339 time carrying the offset you mean (like 2026-10-08T09:00:00+08:00; Z = UTC), in the future and at most 7 days ahead. Either this or after_minutes.

note.description: What to do on waking and where the context is.

worker.name: schedule_wakeup

worker.description: Switch your own model or reasoning effort. Not immediate: this changes the session's setting, which takes effect the next time the session starts (restart or resume); the current turn is unchanged. Use the most expensive tier only when normal tiers clearly fail.

model.description: Model alias such as opus / sonnet.

worker.name: set_session_profile
